missionPremise: The coverage answer is computed correctly upstream and is destroyed in hauska-map before any customer sees it. Verified at source rather than taken from the brief: legacy-design-tools `artifacts/api-server/src/lib/txgioAddressResolve.ts` on origin/main 25d1782f defines `type SitusSearchMissClass = "no-hit" | "out_of_coverage" | "county_out_of_coverage" | "coverage_check_unavailable" | typeof SITUS_SEARCH_BUDGET_ERROR` (line 1179) and returns it with `outOfCoverageState?: string` (line 1194), `outOfCoverageCounty?: {countyFips; countyName; state}` (line 1196) and `coverageCheckUnavailableReason?: string` (line 1198); the route `artifacts/api-server/src/routes/brokeragePlaceSitusSearch.ts` serialises all four (`...(result.outOfCoverageState ? {...} : {})`, `...(result.outOfCoverageCounty ? {...} : {})`, `...(result.coverageCheckUnavailableReason ? {...} : {})`). The map's BFF maps that body to `{ hits }` and nothing else, and the client returns the hit array only, so no class reaches the customer. Ruling basis: OPS-24 Law 1 (the customer predicate is the definition of done) and the mission statement in `_dispatches/2026-09-18_p353-find-box-coverage_dispatch.md`; the owed-answer table there is the same four subjects the customer-leg probe already drives for P-205.
completionPredicate: For each of the four coverage subjects, the property-explorer BFF `GET /api/pe-situs-search` serves `missClass` beside `hits` — `no-hit` for 99999 ZZYZX RD, AUSTIN, TX 78701; `county_out_of_coverage` with outOfCoverageCounty {countyFips 48331, countyName 'Milam County', state 'TX'} for 99999 ZZYZX RD, CAMERON, TX 76520; `county_out_of_coverage` with {48053, 'Burnet County', 'TX'} for 99999 ZZYZX RD, MARBLE FALLS, TX 78654; `out_of_coverage` with outOfCoverageState 'CO' for 1600 BROADWAY, DENVER, CO 80202 — and a query that finds hits serialises byte-for-byte as it did before. The Find box tells the customer which kind of no-result it is in words, and neither Find path can turn an out-of-coverage answer into a geocoded pin. Falsifiable by revert-and-run on fixtures built from those live wire shapes (pre-change drops missClass, post-change carries all four), and after deploy by `node --use-system-ca scripts/surface-probe.mjs --rows P-205` in doc_repo with the map half PASS on all four subjects.
scopeBasis: hauska-map only, one PR, FAN-DEPTH 0 (this lane launched no sub-agents). In scope: the two Find-box data paths and the sentence the customer reads — the BFF core + route (api/_lib/pe-situs-search-core.ts, api/pe-situs-search.ts), the client (src/lib/situs-search-client.ts, src/lib/geocodeClient.ts), the raw-Find identity resolver (src/lib/parcel-lookup.ts), the suggest state machine (src/lib/search-suggest.ts) and the Find bar renderer (src/browse/SearchBar.tsx). Out of scope and named: (1) the cortex-api side, which is already correct and is not touched (legacy-design-tools, a different repo); (2) the MCP's `find_parcel` half of P-205, measured PASS 4 of 4 on 2026-09-18 and not touched; (3) the coverage endpoint `/parcel-record-gate-verdict/coverage/check` (hauska-engine, P-210) — read only as context, not touched; (4) the typeahead's recents/parcel-id fast paths, which cannot produce a coverage answer and are deliberately left as they are (they are named as bypasses in the close, not modified). designDecision.oneWriterOfTheWireShape: api/_lib/pe-situs-search-core.ts stays the single place the upstream body is mapped to the wire, and mapSitusSearchResponse stays its single writer. The route does not re-map (D3 marked unchanged), so there is no second implementation for DEV_PROCESS 2.4 to police.
designDecision.neverFabricate: When the upstream sends no missClass, the BFF emits `{ hits }` exactly as before — an absent class is never invented. When hits are non-empty the body is `{ hits }` byte-for-byte, which is the falsifier's 'a query that finds hits is unchanged'. This is the DECLARED-ABSENCE discipline applied to a miss class: a class we do not have is not written.
designDecision.timeoutIsNotAMiss: A timeout (and any other failure to obtain an answer) is served as `{ hits: [], missClass: 'coverage_check_unavailable', coverageCheckUnavailableReason: '...' }` at HTTP 200, because 'we could not check coverage' IS the fourth owed class and is the honest opposite of a miss. The 5s ceiling is raised because it is too close to the measured path: 3.8s end to end for Cameron on 2026-09-18 (dispatch) leaves ~1.2s of headroom, so a slow-but-answering coverage check was being turned into an outage. The new ceiling is 9000ms, chosen under the probe's own 12s budget for this leg (surface-probe.mjs:1216 `12_000`) so a BFF timeout is still measurable rather than being graded as a dead surface. The unauthenticated/misconfigured case keeps its existing 503 `proxy_not_configured`, which is a deployment fact, not a coverage answer.
designDecision.stopRule: The fall-through stops on exactly the two classes that mean 'this place is outside the coverage area': `county_out_of_coverage` and `out_of_coverage`. It does NOT stop on `no-hit` (a covered miss is a legitimate reason to keep looking down the envelope ladder), nor on `coverage_check_unavailable` (we do not know, so refusing to look would be a worse failure), nor on the budget class. This is the narrowest rule that satisfies 'a geocoded pin must not stand in for we do not cover this county' without changing behaviour where the class carries no coverage claim.
designDecision.whichVariantWins: fetchUniqueSitusPin and the client both fan out over situsQueryVariants. For the miss class the PRIMARY variant (the query as typed) wins when it carries one, else the first variant that does; otherwise there is no class. This mirrors the existing identity rule (the situs index is the identity writer, the caller's own query is the authority) and avoids inventing a precedence table over derived variants that the upstream never ranked. Hits keep their existing union behaviour unchanged — this rule governs only the empty-class answer.
designDecision.oneSentencePerClass: A single pure module (src/lib/coverage-miss.ts) owns (a) reading the class out of a wire body and (b) the sentence the customer reads, so both Find paths and the typeahead say the same words about the same class. `no-hit` reads as a covered miss; `county_out_of_coverage` names county and state; `out_of_coverage` names the state; `coverage_check_unavailable` says the check is unavailable and explicitly refuses to read as 'no results'; an unrecognised class (e.g. upstream's budget refuse) gets a generic 'could not answer' sentence rather than being silently rendered as a miss.
designDecision.typeaheadCorrection: fetchMergedSearchSuggestions currently merges Photon rows unconditionally, so an out-of-coverage address still shows geocoded address rows in the dropdown — a geocoded pin standing in for 'we do not cover this county', which is item 3 in its most-used form. The merged fetcher now drops the geocode contribution when the situs leg reports an out-of-coverage class, and carries the sentence into the dropdown so the reason is visible where the rows are missing.
